title: Scorching Heat Wave to Bake Midwest and East Coast for July 4th
summary: Get ready to sweat! A huge heat wave is heading for the Midwest and East Coast just in time for the Fourth of July. Forecasters say temperatures could reach a sizzling 105 degrees in some places. That's hot enough to fry an egg on the sidewalk! More than 102 million people are under extreme heat warnings. The heat is caused by a "heat dome" — imagine a giant lid trapping hot air over the country. Cities like Chicago, New York, and Washington, D.C. will feel like an oven. The National Weather Service says Thursday and Friday will be the worst days. The heat can be dangerous for everyone, especially older people, kids, and pets. So what can you do? Stay inside when you can, drink lots of water, and take it easy. Some summer camps have already been canceled because it's just too hot. Scientists say climate change is making heat waves like this more common. The planet is warming up, so these super-hot days are happening more often. Even though Saturday might be a little cooler, it's still going to be a scorcher. Stay safe and keep cool!
why_it_matters: This shows that extreme weather can change your holiday fun and even affect your health, so learning how to stay cool and drink enough water is important for you and your family.

background_read: The Fourth of July is a huge national holiday when millions of Americans celebrate outdoors with parades, barbecues, and fireworks.
A heat dome forms when high pressure traps hot air like a lid over a region, and climate change makes these events stronger and more frequent.
The Midwest (states like Illinois and Ohio) and the East Coast (from Maine to Florida) will be hit hardest, including big cities like Chicago and New York.
Article_Structure: WHO: Forecasters, the National Weather Service, 102 million people including kids, older people, and scientists
WHAT: An extreme heat wave caused by a heat dome is bringing temperatures up to 105°F to the Midwest and East Coast right around the Fourth of July, with warnings about health risks.
WHERE: Across the Midwestern and Eastern United States, especially cities like Chicago, New York, and Washington, D.C.
WHY: Because a weather pattern called a heat dome is trapping hot air, and climate change is making such dangerous heat events happen more often.

perspectives.description: They work hard to warn people early so everyone can stay indoors, drink water, and avoid heat sickness, believing that preparation saves lives.
They worry about children being outside in dangerous heat and have canceled summer camps to keep kids safe, even though it disrupts summer plans.
They see this heat wave as more proof of long-term warming: as the planet heats up, these scorching events will grow more intense unless pollution is reduced.
